entities.fact: Bryde's whale is the tropical rorqual, feeding on krill and schooling fish year-round in warm water rather than migrating to the poles.

entities.name: Gray whale
entities.fact: Gray whales mostly suck amphipods from seabed mud, but also gulp swarms of krill and crab larvae, and migrate about 20,000 kilometres a year.

entities.name: Sperm whale
entities.fact: Sperm whales dive more than 2,000 metres and hold their breath for over an hour to hunt squid in the dark, and carry the largest brain of any animal.

entities.name: Crabeater seal
entities.fact: The crabeater seal eats no crabs at all: it strains krill from the water through lobed, interlocking teeth, and is the most numerous seal on Earth.

entities.name: Leopard seal
entities.fact: The leopard seal is famous for hunting penguins, but krill makes up a large part of its diet, sieved through its lobed back teeth.

entities.name: Antarctic fur seal
entities.fact: The Antarctic fur seal feeds mainly on krill around South Georgia, where its numbers rebounded from near extinction to several million.

entities.name: Penguin
entities.fact: Penguins have backward-pointing spines on the tongue and roof of the mouth that stop slippery krill and fish escaping as they swallow.

entities.name: Emperor penguin
entities.fact: Emperor penguins dive deeper than 500 metres for fish, squid and krill, and the males fast for about four months while incubating an egg on their feet.

entities.name: Adélie penguin
entities.fact: Adélie penguins eat mostly krill, and the pink stains of their guano show up from space, letting scientists count colonies by satellite.

entities.name: Gentoo penguin
entities.fact: The gentoo is the fastest-swimming bird, reaching about 36 kilometres per hour, and feeds on krill and fish close to shore.

entities.name: Chinstrap penguin
entities.fact: Chinstrap penguins feed almost entirely on krill, and their numbers have crashed as warming has thinned the krill swarms near the Antarctic Peninsula.

entities.name: Macaroni penguin
entities.fact: Macaroni penguins are the most numerous penguin and together eat more krill than any other seabird species.

entities.name: Rockhopper penguin
entities.fact: Rockhopper penguins hop up cliffs with both feet together and feed on krill, squid and small fish.

entities.name: Wilson's storm petrel
entities.fact: Wilson's storm petrel patters across the water on dangling feet, picking krill and oil from the surface, and may be the most numerous wild bird on Earth.

entities.name: Antarctic prion
entities.fact: The Antarctic prion filters krill through comb-like plates in its bill, like a tiny flying baleen whale, which is why sailors called prions whalebirds.

entities.name: Whale shark
entities.fact: The whale shark, the largest fish, gathers at Ningaloo Reef each year to gulp swarms of krill and fish spawn through a mouth more than a metre wide.

entities.name: Manta ray
entities.fact: Manta rays funnel zooplankton such as krill and copepods into their mouths with two head lobes, sometimes somersaulting in loops through a swarm.

entities.name: Salmon
entities.fact: Pacific salmon at sea feed heavily on krill, and the pigment from those crustaceans is what turns their flesh pink.

entities.name: Herring
entities.fact: Herring feed on copepods and krill in schools of millions, and communicate at night with bursts of bubbles from their vents.

entities.name: Sardine
entities.fact: Sardines filter copepods and krill from the water, and their immense schools off South Africa form the annual sardine run.

entities.name: Atlantic mackerel
entities.fact: Atlantic mackerel feed on copepods and krill as they swim constantly to breathe, and are the species the British fleet catches in the largest quantity.

entities.name: Capelin
entities.fact: Capelin feed on krill and copepods and spawn on beaches in their millions, and almost everything in the North Atlantic, from cod to whales, eats them.

entities.name: Mackerel icefish
entities.fact: The mackerel icefish has no red blood cells, so its blood runs clear, and it feeds almost entirely on Antarctic krill.

entities.name: Antarctic silverfish
entities.fact: The Antarctic silverfish is the key fish of the Antarctic food web, eating krill and copepods and in turn feeding penguins, seals and toothfish.

entities.name: Vent mussel
entities.fact: Vent mussels pack their gills with bacteria that feed them from the vent chemicals, forming beds thousands strong around warm vents and seeps.

entities.name: Vent clam
entities.fact: The giant white vent clam grows to more than 25 centimetres, has bright red flesh full of haemoglobin, and gets its food from bacteria in its gills.

entities.name: Titanic
entities.fact: The Titanic lies in two main pieces about 3,800 metres down in the North Atlantic, where Robert Ballard's team found it in 1985.

entities.name: Lusitania
entities.fact: The Lusitania was torpedoed by a German U-boat off Ireland in 1915 and lies on its side in about 93 metres of water, slowly collapsing.

entities.name: Bismarck
entities.fact: The battleship Bismarck was sunk in May 1941 after a three-day chase, and Robert Ballard found the wreck in 1989 standing upright about 4,700 metres down.

entities.name: Endurance
entities.fact: Shackleton's ship Endurance, crushed by ice in 1915, was found in March 2022 at 3,008 metres in the Weddell Sea, with its name still legible on the stern.

entities.name: Britannic
entities.fact: The Britannic, Titanic's larger sister, struck a mine while serving as a hospital ship in 1916 and lies on its side at about 120 metres off the Greek island of Kea.

entities.name: USS Indianapolis
entities.fact: The USS Indianapolis, sunk by a Japanese submarine in 1945 after delivering atomic bomb parts, was found in 2017 about 5,500 metres down in the Philippine Sea.

entities.name: HMS Hood
entities.fact: HMS Hood blew up and sank in three minutes after a hit from the Bismarck in 1941, with only 3 of 1,418 men surviving; the wreck lies about 2,800 metres down.

entities.name: USS Yorktown
entities.fact: The aircraft carrier USS Yorktown, sunk at the Battle of Midway in 1942, was found by Robert Ballard in 1998 about 5,000 metres down.

entities.name: Andrea Doria
entities.fact: The Italian liner Andrea Doria sank in 1956 after colliding with the Stockholm off Nantucket, and its wreck at about 73 metres is called the Mount Everest of wreck diving.

entities.name: Yamato
entities.fact: The Yamato, the largest battleship ever built, was sunk by US aircraft in April 1945 and lies in two main pieces about 340 metres down off Kyushu.

entities.name: Musashi
entities.fact: The battleship Musashi, sister of the Yamato, was sunk in the Sibuyan Sea in 1944 and found by Paul Allen's team in 2015 more than 1,000 metres down.

entities.name: USS Lexington
entities.fact: The carrier USS Lexington, scuttled after the Battle of the Coral Sea in 1942, was found in 2018 about 3,000 metres down with aircraft still intact on the seabed.

entities.name: USS Thresher
entities.fact: The nuclear submarine USS Thresher was lost with 129 people during deep-diving tests in 1963, and its remains lie about 2,600 metres down off New England.

entities.name: San José
entities.fact: The Spanish galleon San José, sunk by the British off Cartagena in 1708 with a cargo of gold, silver and emeralds, was located in 2015 about 600 metres down.

entities.name: SS Central America
entities.fact: The SS Central America, the 'Ship of Gold', sank in an 1857 hurricane with tonnes of California gold, and was found in 1988 about 2,200 metres down off the Carolinas.

entities.name: USS Scorpion
entities.fact: The nuclear submarine USS Scorpion was lost with 99 crew in May 1968 and lies about 3,000 metres down south-west of the Azores.

entities.name: ARA San Juan
entities.fact: The Argentine submarine ARA San Juan vanished in November 2017 with 44 crew and was found a year later about 900 metres down in the South Atlantic.

entities.name: Akagi
entities.fact: The Japanese carrier Akagi, flagship of the Pearl Harbor attack, was sunk at Midway in 1942 and found in 2019 more than 5,000 metres down.

entities.name: Kaga
entities.fact: The Japanese carrier Kaga, sunk at the Battle of Midway in 1942, was the first Midway carrier wreck found, in October 2019, more than 5,000 metres down.

entities.name: HMAS Sydney
entities.fact: HMAS Sydney was lost with all 645 crew after a battle with the German raider Kormoran in 1941, and was found in 2008 about 2,500 metres down off Western Australia.

entities.name: El Faro
entities.fact: The cargo ship El Faro sank in Hurricane Joaquin in October 2015 with all 33 crew, and was found about 4,600 metres down near the Bahamas.

entities.name: Estonia
entities.fact: The ferry Estonia sank in a Baltic storm in September 1994 with the loss of 852 lives, and lies on the seabed at about 80 metres.

entities.name: MV Derbyshire
entities.fact: The bulk carrier Derbyshire, the largest British ship ever lost at sea, went down in a typhoon in 1980 with 44 people and was found in 1994 about 4,200 metres down.

entities.name: SS Rio Grande
entities.fact: The German blockade runner Rio Grande, sunk in 1944, was found in 1996 at 5,762 metres in the South Atlantic and held the record for the deepest shipwreck for decades.

entities.name: USS Johnston
entities.fact: The destroyer USS Johnston, sunk off Samar in 1944, was surveyed in 2021 at 6,469 metres, briefly the deepest shipwreck ever identified.

entities.name: K-129
entities.fact: The Soviet missile submarine K-129 sank in 1968 about 4,900 metres down in the Pacific; the CIA's Glomar Explorer secretly lifted part of it in 1974 and the rest still lies there.

entities.name: Komsomolets
entities.fact: The Soviet nuclear submarine Komsomolets sank in the Norwegian Sea in 1989 and lies about 1,700 metres down with its reactor and two nuclear torpedoes.

entities.name: SS Gairsoppa
entities.fact: The SS Gairsoppa, torpedoed in 1941, was found in 2011 about 4,700 metres down, and more than 100 tonnes of silver were recovered from it, the deepest such salvage.

entities.name: USS Hornet
entities.fact: The carrier USS Hornet, which launched the Doolittle Raid, was sunk in 1942 and found in 2019 about 5,300 metres down near the Solomon Islands.

entities.name: INS Dakar
entities.fact: The Israeli submarine Dakar vanished in 1968 and was found in 1999 about 2,900 metres down between Crete and Cyprus.

entities.name: USS Samuel B. Roberts
entities.fact: The destroyer escort USS Samuel B. Roberts, sunk off Samar in 1944, was surveyed in 2022 at 6,895 metres, the deepest shipwreck ever identified.

entities.name: Horseshoe crab
entities.fact: Horseshoe crabs are not true crabs at all but ancient relatives of spiders, and their blue, copper-based blood is used to test medicines for bacterial contamination.
